content.title: Why Michael B. Jordan can’t receive dual Oscar nominations for Sinners
content.text: Dual Michael B. Jordans helped make Sinners one of the year's biggest films, but he won't be able to double his pleasure when it comes to Oscar nominations. Despite delivering two standout performances as identical twin brothers Smoke and Stack in the Warner Bros. horror film, Jordan isn't eligible to submit for Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor. That’s because, when it comes to acting nominations, the Oscars recognize the individual, not the individual roles. In other words, Jordan can only be nominated once per film, in either category — but not both. This restriction dates back to a unique moment in Academy Award history. In 1944, Barry Fitzgerald was nominated for both Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor for his single performance in Going My Way. Fitzgerald ended up winning the supporting award (costar Bing Crosby won the lead Oscar), but the unprecedented dual nomination prompted the Motion Picture Academy to change its rules. Since then, no actor has been allowed to receive two nominations for the same performance. A source at the Academy confirms to Gold Derby that this rule also applies to someone playing two different characters in the same movie. However, there have been performers like Cate Blanchett, Jamie Foxx, Holly Hunter, and Julianne Moore who have received two acting nominations in the same year, but for different films — something the rules do allow. When it comes to Sinners, though, Jordan must submit his strongest performance, which will be in the lead category. Based on Gold Derby prediction data, Jordan is on track to earn an Oscar nomination for Best Actor. He currently ranks fourth among contenders, behind Leonardo DiCaprio, Timothée Chalamet, and Jeremy Allen White. He is set to receive the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award at the 41st annual Santa Barbara International Film Festival on Feb. 12. Meanwhile, Sinners currently is third in Gold Derby’s odds for a Best Picture nomination, while director Ryan Coogler holds fourth place in the Best Director race. The film is also on track for nominations in original screenplay, cinematography, casting, film editing, production design, costume design, makeup and hairstyling, sound, and score.
